title: THE GOD WHO TOOK AND LED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'But I took your father Abraham from the land beyond the Euphrates and led him throughout Canaan and gave him many descendants. I gave him Isaac, and to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. I assigned the hill country of Seir to Esau, but Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.'" — Josh 24:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Listen to how many times God says "I" in these verses. "I took your father Abraham." "I led him." "I gave him many descendants." "I gave him Isaac." "I gave Jacob and Esau." Again and again, God is the one acting. Abraham did not find God; God took Abraham. The whole family line unfolded because God was working at every step.

This is the true shape of our salvation. We often imagine that we found God, that we made the decisive move. But Scripture keeps turning our eyes back to His initiative. Jesus said plainly, "You did not choose me, but I chose you" (John 15:16). Before we ever reached for God, He had already reached for us.

There is great rest in this. If your relationship with God began with His "I took" and "I led," then it does not finally depend on the strength of your grip but on His. The God who took hold of Abraham and led him step by step is the same God who took hold of you.

Look back over your own life and you may see the same pattern — God taking, leading, providing, long before you understood what was happening. Give thanks today to the God whose initiative writes every good chapter of your story. He began this work, and He will carry it through.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where can you see God's initiative in your own life story?
2. How does "I chose you" change how you view your relationship with God?
3. Does your security rest on your grip on God, or on His grip on you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You took hold of me before I ever reached for You. Help me to rest in Your initiative and to trust the grip of Your hand on my life. Amen.
